brief: Bernstein surveys 63 outside 2030 U.S. data center capacity forecasts spanning 59-186 GW and attributes the spread to five analyst "seats," each anchored on a different methodology that systematically skews its own output. Infrastructure/REIT investors count sites and skew conservative, yielding 135-167 IT-GW by 2030 (base 142). Industrials analysts extrapolate incremental-addition growth rates and skew higher: 124-242 IT-GW (base 161). Tech analysts derive capacity from hyperscaler capex, landing at a base of 152 IT-GW (range 115-195). Semis analysts derive it from server/hardware shipments: base 149 IT-GW (range 137-160). Labor analysts model available craft labor as a ceiling rather than a demand forecast: 142 GW (range 120-204). Reconciling the five, Bernstein's stated definitive estimate is 149 IT-GW by 2030, adding 19 IT-GW in 2027 and 25 IT-GW in 2028; its PM Summary separately states the most reasonable outcome is closer to ~160 IT-GW, implying over 4.5x growth from 2025 levels. Because today's market is supply constrained, Bernstein favors names with direct exposure to energized capacity over names dependent on AI-adoption pace, and flags the largest risk in valuations already pricing the most aggressive capacity outcomes.
